dedupe_keys.name: europe gnss as critical infrastructure cross sectoral impacts of service interruptions progress in disaster science 2026

description: This case study examines global navigation satellite systems (Galileo, GPS, GLONASS and BeiDou) as critical infrastructure for Europe and maps what an interruption of their positioning and timing services would do to other sectors. Iztok Prezelj and Jelena Juvan published it in Progress in Disaster Science in December 2025, arguing that navigation technology now runs so deep in society that it is critical in its own right. From a synthetic literature review and an expert workshop they identify the dimensions of GNSS criticality (geostrategic and military importance, dual use, broad cross-sectoral application, the ubiquitous timing service of atomic clocks and rising requirements for availability and precision) and the spillover effects on transport, telecommunications and the internet, electric power, finance, agriculture, fisheries, emergency and security services, defence, science, weather monitoring, construction and space operations. Coverage is continental Europe, qualitative. Format and access: an open-access journal article. Licence: CC BY 4.0; free. Caveats: no data were used, so the spillovers are expert judgements, not quantified losses. It supports cascading failure and resilience analysis of GNSS dependency. Related catalogue records are the UK GNSS disruption economic impact study and the January 2016 GPS timing anomaly.
